endorsements.name: Romain Garnier
endorsements.label: CVE-2022-24674
endorsements.description: This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Canon imageCLASS MF644Cdw 10.02 printers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the privet API. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-15834.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: HIGH (CVSS 3.0, 8.8)

endorsements.name: Romain Garnier
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-55108
endorsements.description:
The Control-M/Agent is vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution, arbitrary file read and write and similar unauthorized actions when mutual SSL/TLS authentication is not enabled (i.e. in the default configuration).


NOTE: 

  *  The vendor believes that this vulnerability only occurs when documented security best practices are not followed. BMC has always strongly recommended to use security best practices such as configuring SSL/TLS between Control-M Server and Agent.

  *  The vendor notifies that Control-M/Agent is not impacted in Control-M SaaS
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: CRITICAL (CVSS 3.1, 10)

endorsements.name: Romain Garnier
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-55109
endorsements.description:
An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the out-of-support Control-M/Agent versions 9.0.18 to 9.0.20 and potentially earlier unsupported versions when using an empty or default kdb keystore or a default PKCS#12 keystore. A remote attacker with access to a signed third-party or demo certificate for client authentication can bypass the need for a certificate signed by the certificate authority of the organization during authentication on the Control-M/Agent.

The Control-M/Agent contains hardcoded certificates which are only trusted as fallback if an empty kdb keystore is used; they are never trusted if a PKCS#12 keystore is used. All of these certificates are now expired.


In addition, the Control-M/Agent default kdb and PKCS#12 keystores contain trusted third-party certificates (external recognized CAs and default self-signed demo certificates) which are trusted for client authentication.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: CRITICAL (CVSS 4.0, 9.5)

endorsements.label: CVE-2025-55110

Control-M/Agents use a kdb or PKCS#12 keystore by default, and the default keystore password is well known and documented.

An attacker with read access to the keystore could access sensitive data using this password.

endorsements.name: Romain Garnier
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-55113
endorsements.description: If the Access Control List is enforced by the Control-M/Agent and the C router is in use (default in Out-of-support Control-M/Agent versions 9.0.18 to 9.0.20 and potentially earlier unsupported versions; non-default but configurable using the JAVA_AR setting in newer versions), the verification stops at the first NULL byte encountered in the email address referenced in the client certificate. An attacker could bypass configured ACLs by using a specially crafted certificate.

endorsements.name: Romain Garnier
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-55117
endorsements.description:
A stack-based buffer overflow can be remotely triggered when formatting an error message in the Control-M/Agent when SSL/TLS communication is configured.


The issue occurs in the following cases:

  *  Control-M/Agent 9.0.20: SSL/TLS configuration is set to the non-default setting "use_openssl=n";
  *  Control-M/Agent 9.0.21 and 9.0.22: Agent router configuration uses the non-default settings "JAVA_AR=N" and "use_openssl=n".
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 4.0, 6.3)
